history: 61-year-old man with 4 weeks of worsening headache, personality change and new left-sided weakness.
question: MRI brain with contrast (axial T1 post-gadolinium): findings?
key: A large intra-axial mass with thick, irregular ring enhancement around a necrotic centre, surrounding vasogenic oedema and mass effect — typical of glioblastoma.
credit: Data from The Cancer Imaging Archive, UPENN-GBM collection (CC BY 4.0), doi:10.7937/TCIA.709X-DN49

history: 64-year-old man, 40 pack-years, having lung cancer screening. No symptoms.
question: Low-dose CT chest (lung windows): findings?
key: One or more well-defined soft-tissue nodules in the lung parenchyma — a pulmonary nodule to characterise by size, density and margin (Fleischner / Lung-RADS follow-up).
credit: Data from The Cancer Imaging Archive, LIDC-IDRI collection (CC BY 3.0), doi:10.7937/K9/TCIA.2015.LO9QL9SX

history: 63-year-old man with hepatitis B cirrhosis, rising alpha-fetoprotein and weight loss.
question: CT abdomen (liver protocol): findings?
key: A focal liver mass in a cirrhotic liver, enhancing in the arterial phase with washout later — hepatocellular carcinoma.
credit: Data from The Cancer Imaging Archive, TCGA-LIHC collection (CC BY 3.0), doi:10.7937/K9/TCIA.2016.IMMQW8UQ

history: 66-year-old woman, a year after surgery for colon cancer, with a rising CEA.
question: CT abdomen, portal venous phase: findings?
key: Multiple hypodense lesions in the liver, some with a faint enhancing rim — liver metastases.
credit: Data from The Cancer Imaging Archive, Colorectal-Liver-Metastases collection (CC BY 4.0), doi:10.7937/QXK2-QG03

history: 48-year-old woman with gradual hearing loss and tinnitus in one ear, and unsteadiness.
question: MRI internal auditory meati (high-resolution T2): findings?
key: A well-defined mass in the internal auditory canal extending into the cerebellopontine angle ('ice-cream cone') — vestibular schwannoma.
credit: Data from The Cancer Imaging Archive, Vestibular-Schwannoma-MC-RC collection (CC BY 4.0), doi:10.7937/HRZH-2N82

history: 30-year-old kidney donor having a routine work-up scan. No symptoms.
question: CT abdomen with contrast: any abnormality?
key: Normal liver, pancreas, kidneys, spleen and bowel; no mass, collection or free fluid.
credit: Data from The Cancer Imaging Archive, Pancreas-CT collection (CC BY 3.0), doi:10.7937/K9/TCIA.2016.tNB1kqBU

history: 57-year-old man with painless visible haematuria and weight loss.
question: CT abdomen with contrast: findings?
key: A solid, heterogeneously enhancing mass arising from the kidney, distorting its contour — typical of clear-cell renal cell carcinoma.
credit: Data from The Cancer Imaging Archive, TCGA-KIRC collection (CC BY 3.0), doi:10.7937/K9/TCIA.2016.V6PBVTDR

history: 52-year-old man with 8 days of fever, dry cough and breathlessness; SpO₂ 89% on air.
question: CT chest (lung windows): findings?
key: Bilateral, peripheral, posterior ground-glass opacities with some consolidation — the typical pattern of COVID-19 pneumonia.
credit: Data from The Cancer Imaging Archive, COVID-19-AR collection (CC BY 4.0), doi:10.7937/tcia.2020.py71-5978
